note: Adapted from Hill's 1925 original English description; the original reads Calotermes (Cryptotermes) secundus n. sp.; type locality Northern Territory: Darwin, the description based on a small colony taken from the trunk of a living coconut palm previously attacked by a weevil (Diocalandria) (G. F. H., 8/5/13); a second colony, of young nymphs and larvae only, was taken in the stem of a dead shrub near Darwin at East Point (13/10/15). In both cases only a small part of the host was damaged, in accordance with the usual habit of Cryptotermes, and with no gallery to the ground. The type soldier and associated nymphs are in the National Museum of Victoria. The original describes only the soldier; the alate is unknown.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Closely related to Planocryptotermes nocens Light (paratype examined), but the frons has longitudinal ridges and the shape of the frontal margin differs. It differs from C. (Cryptotermes) primus Hill in the projecting frontal margin, which is broadly concave seen from in front or behind, with two shallow grooves on each side of the middle and with longitudinal ridges running from the clypeo-frontal suture up to the frontal margin; the angular processes on the lower lateral margins of the head and the process on the anterodorsal margin of the antennal socket also differ; in addition the anterior margin of the pronotum has fewer angles and fewer serrations and narrows more towards the posterior margin on both sides.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head yellow posteriorly, becoming darker anteriorly, almost black at the frontal margin; mandibles chestnut brown; pronotum, antennae, labrum and base of head the same colour. Head very short and wide, with a shagreened sculpture, scattered with long setae. Frontal margin projecting (especially at the sides), broadly concave seen from in front or behind, with two shallow grooves on each side of the middle; frontal depression rough, sloping towards the base of the clypeus, with a distinct longitudinal ridge on each side level with the lateral margins of the clypeus, running from the clypeo-frontal suture up to the frontal margin. The lower lateral margin of the head is prolonged into a blunt angular process directed upwards and forwards at about 45° to the head axis, scarcely reaching the tip of antennal segment 2; above this process there is another similar but shorter process, the prolongation of the anterodorsal margin of the antennal socket. Clypeus short and very wide (0.49), anterior margin cream-coloured, slightly arched. Labrum short and wide, pale orange-yellow, with a tuft of moderately long pale setae in the middle. Antennae 13-segmented, segment 1 short and stout, widest at the tip; segment 2 more than half as long as segment 1, one-sixth narrower; segment 3 about as long as segment 2, slightly wider; segments 4 and 5 slightly more than half as long as segments 2 and 3, less contracted at the base; segments 6 and 7 a little longer, about as wide as segments 4 and 5 but more nearly spherical. Cervical sclerite scarcely darker than the base of the head. Anterior margin of the pronotum thickened and dark, markedly convex in the middle and faintly serrate, the middle slightly raised and distinctly lifted towards the sides, the anterior lateral angles, lateral margins and posterior lateral angles rounded, the posterior margin faintly wavy in the middle, with sparse moderately long setae. Legs short and stout, spurs serrate. Measurements: total length (dry specimen) 4.50 mm; head with mandibles 1.99 mm; head from posterior margin to frontal margin 1.14 mm; head width 1.19 mm; head height 0.85 mm; pronotum length 0.85 mm, width 1.14 mm; hind tibia length 0.70 mm.
